innate

/in-AYT/ — rhymes with create or fate · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Innate describes a quality or ability a person or animal is born with, rather than one they learned.

Her innate sense of pitch showed before she ever took a lesson.

Example

Her innate sense of melody allowed her to hum new songs in tune, even before learning to read music.

Innate is precise here because it shows the ability existed from birth. If we just said she had a 'natural sense' of melody, it would be less clear that this was inborn rather than something she picked up from listening to others.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

inborn: Inborn and innate both mean present from birth, and they are the closest pair on this card. The real difference is register: inborn is the plain, everyday word, while innate is the more formal, scientific-sounding choice — the one a psychology textbook or a biologist would reach for.

inherent: Inherent means built into the basic, essential nature of a thing — and the thing can be anything: a plan, a material, a sport. Innate is reserved for living creatures and the traits they are born with. A puppy's herding urge is innate; a diamond's hardness is inherent.

instinctive: Instinctive describes an automatic action done without thinking — flinching at a loud noise, catching a falling cup. Innate describes where a trait came from: born in rather than learned. An instinctive reaction happens in the moment; an innate gift has been part of you from the start.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

learned: gained through study, teaching, or instruction

acquired: picked up gradually through practice and experience

Where it sits · how little training it took to appear

acquired → developed → natural → innate

acquired vs. innate: Acquired sits at the opposite end of the scale from innate: an acquired skill is gained entirely through experience, while an innate ability is present from birth.

developed vs. innate: Developed is still far from innate: a developed talent has been built up through years of practice, while an innate talent needs no training to appear.

natural vs. innate: Natural is just below innate on this scale: a natural talent shows up without teaching or special effort, though it may have been soaked up from early exposure, while an innate ability was already there at birth, before any experience at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-: in, into (not the 'not' prefix) (Latin)

Root — nat (nasci): to be born (Latin)

Put it together: Here in- means 'in' — not the 'not' prefix from words like inept: innate is literally 'born in,' from Latin nasci/natus, 'to be born,' describing a quality built into you from birth rather than learned.

Use the root in a new word: prenatal: The clinic tapes a reminder about the next prenatal visit inside each patient's folder - the same nat- root that makes innate mean 'born in' you.

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Innate describes a quality or ability someone was born with, not something they learned or developed. Use innate when you want to emphasize that something is part of a person from the very beginning. For abilities developed through work, 'acquired' or 'developed' is clearer.
